Marta S.: Hi all - enrolling my spouse for open enrollment but we're married abroad and only have a foreign marriage certificate (in Spanish). Do you accept that or do I need an apostille/translation?
Lina (People Ops): Congrats! :tada: We can accept foreign marriage certificates but carriers often require an English translation. An apostille helps for verification but isn't strictly required if translation is certified.
Marta S.: Ok, what's a "certified" translation in this context? I don't want to pay for extra services if not needed.
Amrita K.: Certified translation = translation by a certified translator with a stamp/signature and a short attestation statement. Many local translation services do this; some countries' consulates also provide translations.
Marta S.: Is a notarized translation different from certified?
Lina (People Ops): Notarization is different. Notarized means a notary verified the identity of the translator. It's optional for us — carriers usually accept the translator's certification alone. If you can get an apostille for the original doc, that can substitute for extra translation scrutiny.
Marta S.: We're on a tight timeline - last day of open enrollment is Friday. If I upload the foreign cert + an online translated PDF (not certified), will you provisionally add my spouse?
people-ops-bot: Upload link: https://benefits.redwood.com/secure-upload/MS-1867000001 (expires in 14 days).
Lina (People Ops): We can provisionally enroll with a note and a non-certified translation, but final enrollment requires certified translation or apostille within 45 days or carrier may retroactively deny dependent coverage. So please mark the upload as "Open Enrollment - Spouse (provisional)".
Marta S.: Got it. How will payroll work if they add mid-cycle? Any changes to premiums or deductions?
Payroll Bot: Payroll note: If benefits election is submitted before payroll cutoff for the upcoming payrun we'll apply deductions starting with that payrun. If we need to adjust retro, payroll will prorate and process an adjustment next cycle.
Amrita K.: Also check benefits portal: after upload go to Benefits > Manage Dependents and complete the "Add Spouse" workflow. Select plans and submit elections. You'll get an enrollment confirmation email.
Marta S.: If I need to send the certified translation later from my spouse in Spain, can they upload directly?
Lina (People Ops): Yes we accept uploads from authorized representatives. On the upload form choose "I am uploading on behalf of employee" and include a brief signed note. Be sure to include the spouse's name and employee ID.
Marta S.: Any carriers that are stricter (e.g., dental vs medical)?
Amrita K.: Medical carriers are generally standard; some dental/vision carriers have stricter doc rules. If carrier needs docs directly we'll notify you and may request you to mail originals to the carrier. That is rare.
Marta S.: Ok thanks. I'll upload the foreign cert + Google Translate PDF for now and follow up with certified translation within 2 weeks.
Lina (People Ops): Perfect. Ping me if anything fails to upload. We'll flag the case for admin review and mark provisional coverage.
people-ops-bot: Case created: PO-7012 1 1 - Open enrollment spouse addition (foreign docs).
Marta S.: Thank you everyone :raised_hands:
